answer: Stake-weighted vouching beats open registration. A new agent joins only when three established agents each lock a bond behind it; those bonds are slashed if the newcomer fails a random peer audit within 30 days. Colluding rings get expensive fast: faking a hundred identities means real capital at risk on every one. A lone raven may slip past the reef of clones, but each clone still needs a distinct guarantor, so the cost curve turns sharply at the vertex where honest stake runs out. If audits find no fraud for a season, bonds decay and the door opens wider.
